subject: Subsetting unmarkedMultFrame to analyze subset of sites

messages.author: 3295392e7ef5938d
messages.subject: Subsetting unmarkedMultFrame to analyze subset of sites
parts:
Hi,

I am wondering if it is possible to subset an unmarkedMultFrame after the fact (after the object is created) in order to analyze only a subset of sites (for example, I have sites in forest and pasture, and would like to run some analyses on pasture sites only). Until now I have just done this by selecting pasture data only prior to making the unmarkedMultFrame, but I would love to know if there is a (more efficient) way to do this after the unmarkedMultFrame has been put together. 

I figured out how to subset part of the unmarkedMultFrame (siteCovs) that contains the variable "hab_type" (pasture vs forest), but I don't know how to get the same subset of points from all the other parts of the unmarkedMultFrame object:

umfs_det_covs$umf[[1]]@siteCovs %>%
  filter(hab_type == "potrero")

Thank you very much!

Anna Lello-Smith

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Subsetting unmarkedMultFrame to analyze subset of sites
parts:
Hi Anna,

Something like this should work:

umf.pot <- umf[siteCovs(umf)$hab_type=="potrero",]

Richard

parts:
That’s a good point. I guess I would handle this by dropping levels (with a warning) in getDesign() where the design matrices are created. I think there are good reasons for keeping relic factor levels around. That said, I’m not going to have time to hack on this, and I’d support any reasonable change that deals with it.

 

In the meantime, Anna, you can remove unused factor levels using code like this:

 

siteCovs(umf.sub) <- droplevels(siteCovs(umf.sub))

From: Ken Kellner
Sent: Monday, November 25, 2019 4:52 PM
To: unmarked
Subject: Re: [unmarked] Subsetting unmarkedMultFrame to analyze subset of sites

 

[External Sender]

However, if you then try to fit a model with the subset unmarkedFrame that includes the factor in question as a covariate (with a level that doesn't appear in the data), you'll probably get a singular Hessian error.

 


On Monday, November 25, 2019 at 4:46:09 PM UTC-5, Richard Chandler wrote:

Hi Chris,

 

In this case, all factor levels are retained, which I think is the desired behavior.

 

Richard

I am wondering if it is possible to subset an unmarkedMultFrame after the fact (after the object is created) in order to analyze only a subset of sites (for example, I have sites in forest and pasture, and would like to run some analyses on pasture sites only). umfs_det_covs$umf[[1]]@siteCovs %>%

Thank you very much!

 

Anna Lello-Smith
